report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/kairos/gated_writes.py: module docstring, rebase helpers, GatedCandidate, artifact root, relay gate, recording runner, provider receipt, spec_for start. Claims enumerated.
risks: 0 | medium | Module docstring claims PHASE 2 promotion is guarded by ONE cross-process lock, but _PromotionLock is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify uniqueness or cross-process behavior here. | Inspect the _PromotionLock definition in a later chunk.

0 | medium | Module docstring claims a held candidate's attempt branch is reaped before run_write_wave returns and that persistence is load-bearing; neither run_write_wave nor TaskAttempt._persist is in this chunk. | Inspect run_write_wave and TaskAttempt._persist definitions.

0 | medium | Module docstring claims Phase 2 re-gates cumulatively after every apply and re-attempts stale candidates; the promote_candidates function is not in this chunk. | Inspect promote_candidates in a later chunk.

0 | medium | Module docstring claims _PromotionLock uses the same msvcrt/fcntl pattern as _BudgetLock and _RoomLock; none of those are visible here. | Inspect _PromotionLock and referenced lock implementations.

0 | low | _relay_gate's docstring claims the gate is judged by offload()'s own verdict and not a second test run; the gate only checks action/wrote and does not run tests, but the claim that offload's verify is the authority depends on offload_runner behavior not visible here. | Inspect offload_runner and TaskAttempt gate invocation.

0 | low | _recording_runner's docstring claims box["result"] is set before TaskAttempt calls the gate, citing _run_with_ledger; that ordering is not visible in this chunk. | Inspect TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger.

0 | low | _provider_receipt's projection is lossy by design; if detail is not a Mapping, returns None and the write-wave projection may collapse provider refusals, which the docstring says it was meant to fix. | Inspect callers of _provider_receipt to see how None is handled.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, declared-path rebasing, GatedCandidate dataclass, artifact root, relay gate, recording runner, provider receipt, and start of _spec_for.

symbols.name: _DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Fallback timeout for curated command gate; 900.0 seconds.

symbols.name: rebase_declared_path
symbols.note: Rebases an absolute path under primary_root to repo-relative POSIX; returns unchanged otherwise.

symbols.name: rebase_declared_paths
symbols.note: Maps rebase_declared_path over a list of paths, returning a tuple.

symbols.name: GatedCandidate
symbols.note: Dataclass holding assignment, spec, and result from Phase 1.

symbols.name: _artifact_root_for
symbols.note: Returns a checkout-external archive directory under LOCALAPPDATA or tempdir, namespaced by repo path hash.

symbols.name: _relay_gate
symbols.note: Returns a TaskAttempt gate closure that judges by offload result action/wrote from a shared box.

symbols.name: _recording_runner
symbols.note: Wraps offload_runner to record its result in a box; returns (runner, box).

symbols.name: _provider_receipt
symbols.note: Projects a small operational dict from an offload runner result's runner_detail.

symbols.name: _spec_for
symbols.note: Starts constructing a TaskSpec for one assignment; body truncated in this chunk.

claims.text: This module does not repeat any of that. It has two responsibilities: PHASE 1 -- CONCURRENT GATING ... PHASE 2 -- PROMOTION ... PHASE 3 -- SEALED HANDOFF
claims.why: The chunk only shows Phase 1 helpers; Phase 2 and Phase 3 functions are not in this chunk, so the claimed responsibilities cannot be fully verified.

claims.text: Output: one GatedCandidate per assignment, each carrying an AttemptResult whose .artifact is a PatchArtifact (inert bytes) when the candidate is clean.
claims.why: GatedCandidate is defined but the code that produces it (gate_candidates) is not in this chunk; PatchArtifact is not referenced here.

claims.text: The primary checkout is untouched -- that is TaskAttempt's own structural guarantee, not something re-implemented or re-verified here.
claims.why: TaskAttempt is not visible in this chunk; no code here touches the primary checkout.

claims.text: run_write_wave additionally asks Phase 1 to persist those bytes in the checkout-external Daedalus artifact archive.
claims.why: run_write_wave is not in this chunk, and _artifact_root_for only returns a path; no persistence call is visible.

claims.text: That is load-bearing for a held candidate: its attempt branch is reaped before this function returns, so an in-memory-only patch could not honestly be described as waiting for review.
claims.why: TaskAttempt reaping and run_write_wave behavior are not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Landing N candidates is itself a shared-mutable-state problem ... so promotion is: guarded by ONE cross-process lock (_PromotionLock ...), applied into ONE dedicated "integration" worktree ... cumulatively RE-GATED after every apply ... and for any candidate whose artifact was captured against a base the integration branch has since moved past ... RE-ATTEMPTED ...
claims.why: promote_candidates and _PromotionLock are not defined in this chunk; none of the promotion machinery is visible.

claims.text: _PromotionLock, the same msvcrt/fcntl pattern as daedalus.budget._BudgetLock and runs/council/room.py's _RoomLock, independently written here because both of those are private to modules this file does not own
claims.why: _PromotionLock is not defined in this chunk; _BudgetLock and _RoomLock are not visible.

claims.text: This is a deliberate correction ... to an earlier draft that proposed git apply --check as the sole conflict detector: a check that passes only proves the bytes still match: it does not prove the SEMANTIC content is still correct once an earlier candidate has landed ahead of it.
claims.why: The correction is described as historical and the actual promotion code is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The adopted Iron Plan closes that path: a write wave may gate and persist candidates, but it always returns them held. promote_candidates remains a separate explicit owner operation.
claims.why: run_write_wave and promote_candidates are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Mirrors daedalus.spine.attempt.DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S without importing it at module scope -- this module imports spine.attempt lazily inside functions (see _spec_for/_attempt_assignment) and adding a top-level import would change that deliberate import order.
claims.why: The chunk shows no top-level import of spine.attempt; _spec_for imports inside the function body (line ~181), and _relay_gate imports GateResult inside the closure (line ~123). The constant is defined at module scope.

claims.text: An absolute path that resolves under primary_root is rebased to its repo-relative form. An absolute path that resolves OUTSIDE primary_root is returned unchanged.
claims.why: Lines 100-106: p.resolve().relative_to(primary_root.resolve()) succeeds for under-root paths and returns as_posix(); ValueError falls through to return raw.

claims.text: spec is retained (not just result) because AttemptResult does not carry the originating TaskSpec -- and Phase 2's staleness retry needs to re-attempt the SAME instruction/target_paths against a NEW base_revision, which requires the original spec, not just its result.
claims.why: GatedCandidate has a spec field, but the claim that AttemptResult lacks the spec and that Phase 2 uses it cannot be verified without AttemptResult and promote_candidates.

claims.text: A held candidate cannot live only in AttemptResult.artifact: run_write_wave returns plain dictionaries and TaskAttempt reaps its candidate branch, so those bytes otherwise disappear as soon as the call returns.
claims.why: run_write_wave and TaskAttempt are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Keep the archive beside the worktree/control state, namespaced by checkout identity, and let TaskAttempt._persist apply its primary-tree fence before it creates or writes anything.
claims.why: TaskAttempt._persist is not visible; _artifact_root_for only computes a path, no write happens here.

claims.text: A gate callable only ever receives a RunnerContext (worktree/branch/base/task/is_cancelled) -- never the runner's return value -- so there is no direct way to ask "did offload() call this clean".
claims.why: The gate signature and RunnerContext are not visible in this chunk; the closure takes ctx but does not use it.

claims.text: box is a mutable cell the paired runner (_recording_runner) writes its result into before returning; this closure reads it back.
claims.why: _recording_runner sets box["result"] immediately after base_runner returns (line 148), and _relay_gate's _gate reads box.get("result") (line 125).

claims.text: Why not TaskAttempt's own default (pytest_gate(task.gate_paths), a bare python -m pytest)? It assumes pytest, which is not every project's test runner -- offload()'s own verify() already runs the PROJECT'S configured test_command, whatever that is. Running it again here would be a SECOND, independent verify of the same change, which is the "raw provider call" the standing orders say must not happen: offload's verify+rollback cascade is meant to stay the one authority for per-task correctness.
claims.why: offload()'s verify behavior and the 'standing orders' are external to this chunk; the gate itself does not run tests, but the claim about offload's authority is not verifiable here.

claims.text: This still catches a real failure mode a bare "is the diff non-empty" check would miss: offload can finish with action == "escalated_after_verify_fail" while wrote is NON-EMPTY ... and only checking action == "offloaded" (not "artifact exists") refuses it.
claims.why: The gate checks action == "offloaded" and bool(wrote), which would refuse escalated_after_verify_fail, but the claim about offload's behavior is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Returns (runner, box). box["result"] is set the instant the runner returns, which is always BEFORE TaskAttempt calls the gate (see daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger: runner, then artifact capture, then gate) -- so _relay_gate reading box always sees this attempt's own result, never a stale or missing one.
claims.why: The ordering claim depends on TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger, which is not in this chunk; the local code does set box before returning, but the gate call ordering is external.

claims.text: The full provider result lives on AttemptResult.runner_detail.
claims.why: AttemptResult is not defined in this chunk; the code reads getattr(result, "runner_detail", None), which would be None if absent, but the claim that the full result lives there is external.

claims.text: The write-wave projection used to drop it, collapsing every provider refusal into "the runner produced no change to gate".
claims.why: Historical behavior and write-wave callers are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Keep only routing/action facts, measured writes, and rewrite activation/skip provenance -- never prompts, repository content, or arbitrary model prose.
claims.why: The code copies only specific keys: provider, model, action, wrote, did_work, report_status, verify, and handoff keys windowed_rewrite, skipped, slice_context_dropped. It does not copy arbitrary content.

observations.what: rebase_declared_path returns raw string unchanged for relative and outside-root absolute paths; the docstring says outside-root is left for downstream guards, but relative paths are also returned unchanged without comment.
_artifact_root_for uses LOCALAPPDATA or tempdir, not a path beside worktree/control state as the docstring claims.
_relay_gate returns a gate that does not use its ctx argument; the gate's passed depends solely on box contents, which are set by _recording_runner.
_provider_receipt returns None when runner_detail is missing or not a Mapping, which could collapse provider refusals into 'no change' downstream, contradicting the docstring's intent to avoid that.
The chunk starts _spec_for but its body is truncated; import of TaskSpec is lazy inside the function, consistent with the module comment.
